chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad ibn al-Hasan al-Qizwini, Abu al-Hasan known as Ibn Maqbara, narrated to us from Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Aamir from Essam ibn Yusuf... from Muhammad ibn Ayyoub al-Kelabi, from Amr ibn Sulaiman, from Abdullah ibn Imran, from Ali ibn Zaid, from Saeed ibn al-Musayyab, from Zaid ibn Thabit, who said:

The Prophet (peace be upon him and his family) said: Whoever loves Ali in his lifetime and after his death, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, will record for him security and faith as long as the sun rises and sets. long as the sun rises and sets. And whoever hates him in his lifetime and after his death, will die a death of ignorance (Jahiliyyah) and will be called to account for his deeds.

key_terms.حُوسِبَ: He will be called to account

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual consequence of loving or hating Imam Ali (AS) according to this hadith?
ai.summary: Recorded by Shaykh al-Saduq in Fadail al-Shia, this hadith establishes the love for Imam Ali (AS) as a definitive criterion for true faith, linking it to the preservation of 'al-Amn wa al-Iman' (security and faith) throughout one's life. It contrasts this with the state of 'Jahiliyyah' for those who harbor enmity, emphasizing that such hatred invalidates one's spiritual standing and leads to specific divine accountability.
